findings.excerpt:
/-- The arity components of `coderiv F` are the restrictions of `F` to each tensor length. -/
@[simp]
theorem taylorComponent_coderiv (F : ReducedTensorWords R M →ₗ[R] M)
    (n : {n : ℕ // 0 < n}) :
    taylorComponent (coderiv R F) n = F ∘ₗ of R M n := by
  rw [taylorComponent, letter_comp_coderiv]
findings.problem: `taylorComponent_coderiv` and `taylorComponent_apply` (lines 523-528) are competing simp rules for the same term `taylorComponent (coderiv R F) n x`, and they produce different normal forms. `taylorComponent_apply` rewrites any `taylorComponent b n x` to `letter R M (b (of R M n x))`, so whenever that rule is used (typically in a `simp only` list that omits the coderiv-specific rule) the term becomes `letter R M (coderiv R F (of R M n x))`, and nothing in the simp set closes it: `letter_comp_coderiv` (lines 432-434) is stated for the composite `letter R M ∘ₗ coderiv R F`, and `LinearMap.comp_apply` only unfolds composites into applications, never folds an application back into a composite. The same gap exists for `letter_comp_coderiv` alone: the file supplies the composite form but no applied form `letter R M (coderiv R F (of R M n z)) = F (of R M n z)`. Downstream proofs show the cost: after `simp only [LinearMap.taylorComponent_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply]` they have to re-fold the composite by hand.
findings.proposed_change:
Add the pointwise companion lemma (proof by `LinearMap.congr_fun`), e.g.

@[simp]
theorem letter_coderiv_of (F : ReducedTensorWords R M →ₗ[R] M) (n : {n : ℕ // 0 < n})
    (z : TensorPower R n.1 M) :
    letter R M (coderiv R F (of R M n z)) = F (of R M n z) :=
  LinearMap.congr_fun (letter_comp_coderiv R F) (of R M n z)

and keep (or additionally state pointwise) `taylorComponent_coderiv` as
`taylorComponent (coderiv R F) n z = F (of R M n z)`. Both have hypothesis-free left-hand sides, so neither competes with nor loops against `taylorComponent_apply`, `letter_comp_coderiv` or `LinearMap.comp_apply`.
findings.benefit: After the standard `taylorComponent_apply`/`comp_apply` normalisation the goal `letter R M (coderiv R F (of R M n x)) = ...` is closed automatically instead of being a dead end, so the result of simplifying a `taylorComponent` of a Taylor expansion no longer depends on which of the two competing rules the simplifier reaches first. The same applied lemma is what the graded analogue needs: `taylorComponent_gradedCoderiv` and `taylorComponent_comp_gradedCoderiv_of_tprod` currently have to insert `rw [← LinearMap.comp_apply (letter R M), letter_comp_gradedCoderiv]`, i.e. they undo the simplifier's orientation by hand.

findings.excerpt:
def IsCoderivation (b : ReducedTensorWords R M →ₗ[R] ReducedTensorWords R M) : Prop :=
  deconcatenation R M ∘ₗ b =
    (LinearMap.rTensor (ReducedTensorWords R M) b +
        LinearMap.lTensor (ReducedTensorWords R M) b) ∘ₗ deconcatenation R M
findings.problem: The body of `IsCoderivation` keeps the sum outside the composition, `(rTensor b + lTensor b) ∘ₗ deconcatenation`, which is the reverse of the simplifier's normal form for `LinearMap.add_comp` (`(f + g) ∘ₗ h` rewrites to `f ∘ₗ h + g ∘ₗ h`, never back). It is also a different shape from the hypothesis expected by the shared twist lemma `eq_of_letter_comp_eq_of_twist` (lines 269-279) and from the graded predicate it is meant to specialise. As a result every conversion in the tau = id case is an anti-simp rewrite: `IsCoderivation.eq_of_letter_comp_eq` needs `rw [isCoderivation_iff] at h₁; rwa [LinearMap.rTensor_id, LinearMap.comp_id, ← LinearMap.add_comp]` twice (lines 319-322), and `IsCoderivation.isGradedCoderivation` in GradedCoderivation.lean needs the same `← LinearMap.add_comp`. By contrast, the graded analogue is stored distributed, which is why `IsGradedCoderivation.eq_of_letter_comp_eq` can pass its hypotheses to `eq_of_letter_comp_eq_of_twist` verbatim.
findings.proposed_change: Either state the body distributed, `deconcatenation R M ∘ₗ b = LinearMap.rTensor (ReducedTensorWords R M) b ∘ₗ deconcatenation R M + LinearMap.lTensor (ReducedTensorWords R M) b ∘ₗ deconcatenation R M` (and word `isCoderivation_iff` the same way), or add a bridge lemma giving exactly that distributed identity so consumers can `simpa only [ReducedTensorWords.map_id, LinearMap.rTensor_id, LinearMap.comp_id] using h` instead of `rw [← LinearMap.add_comp]`. In either case, the tau = id instance of `eq_of_letter_comp_eq_of_twist`'s hypothesis becomes `IsCoderivation R b` up to `map_id`/`rTensor_id`/`comp_id`.
findings.benefit: The ungraded predicate then agrees with the simp normal form of `LinearMap.add_comp` and with the shape of `IsGradedCoderivation`, so the four existing `← LinearMap.add_comp` call sites stop undoing the simplifier, and the ungraded `eq_of_letter_comp_eq` / `isGradedCoderivation` conversions reduce to `simp`-only steps symmetric with the graded versions.
